issue.title: Thinking tags inside a save block silently prevent tool execution

steps:
In the current working directory, create a file named prompt_template.xml for our LLM evaluation harness. Its content must be exactly the following template (keep every tag and line as-is):

<system>
so Assume You are a careful math tutor.
</system>
<instructions>
Before answering, reason inside the thinking tags, then give only the final number inside the answer tags.
</instructions>
<thinking>
Work through the problem step by step here.
</thinking>
<answer>
Final numeric answer here.
</answer>
Please show me the exact current content of prompt_template.xml as it is on disk, so I can verify it was created correctly.
expected: The save block is executed and prompt_template.xml is written with the exact template, or a failure is reported instead of being silently ignored.
defect: The model's well-formed save block (and any following shell block) is never executed: no 'Saved to' result, no prompt_template.xml on disk, and the ACP turn ends with end_turn.

fault location.explanation: Finds the first `</thinking>` anywhere in the reply and, because a line-start `<thinking>` exists before it (inside the save block's content), discards everything up to and including that tag, cutting the save block's opening fence away.
The unclosed-thinking early exit also matches `<thinking>` at a line start inside a code fence and returns without extracting any block.

Root cause: INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). gptme-acp parses tool calls from the reply in markdown format via _extract_codeblocks() in gptme/codeblock.py. Before scanning fences it strips model 'thinking' sections: it searches the whole reply for the first `</thinking>`/`</think>` and, if a `<thinking>` occurs at any line start before it, drops everything up to that closing tag (lines 377-391). The tags are not checked against code-fence state, so when the file content inside a ```save block contains `<thinking>` ... `</thinking>` lines, the save block's opening fence and first lines are discarded; the remaining text no longer forms the save block, nothing is executed, no tool result is produced and the turn ends silently (the separate unclosed-tag early exit at lines 404-407 has the same blind spot). Minimal fix: only treat thinking tags as section markers when they appear at a line start outside any code fence, which is what the still-open PR https://github.com/gptme/gptme/pull/4491 (commit 91bcdd797, `_is_standalone_outside_fences`) proposes; it is not merged.
